record.question: Why are airplane windows rounded, and what did the Comet investigation actually find?
record.audience_reason: Everyone has sat next to an airplane window; the popular 'square windows' story is half right, and the full version teaches a general engineering idea (stress concentration and fatigue).

editorial_contribution.statement: We walk the 1954 evidence in order (pressurized cabin, the Farnborough tank test at ~3,060 cycles, the Elba roof-window wreckage), show force in the skin detouring and piling up at a cut-out's tightest turn, put a number on it with a labeled Inglis model (round hole = 3x; tighter tip = higher), and correct the myth: the Comet's windows had 3-inch corner radii, but the stress there ran far higher than calculated.

record.custom_scene: A manila case file with two flights and a red-ringed window corner; a breathing cabin cross-section; a fuselage in a water tank with a cycle counter and a crack growing from a hatch corner; a torn roof panel with fatigue beach marks; force-flow lines bunching at a cut-out's corners; a live Inglis curve with a morphing hole; the real window drawn to scale with its 3-inch radius; a squarish window morphing into an oval traced by a highlighter.

cover_composition.main_object: case folder with a jet silhouette and a red-ringed window corner

record.sources_and_assumptions: See sources-and-rights.md. The stress model is labeled on screen as a simplified elliptical-hole model, shape only, not the Comet's numbers; the force-flow lines are an illustration.
record.asset_provenance: All visuals drawn in code for this episode; no archive photos; Inter (OFL); DejaVu Sans Mono (Bitstream Vera license); narration Kokoro (Apache-2.0); sound effects synthesized.

scenes.subject: case folder: two Comet flights with dates, a red ring around a window corner

explain.understand: two jets broke up; the answer will be a window corner

scenes.tts: In 1954, two Comet jetliners broke apart in flight, months apart. The clue was the corner of a window.
scenes.caption: In 1954, two Comet jetliners broke apart in flight,|months apart.|The clue was the corner of a window.

scenes.subject: Exhibit 1: cabin cross-section swelling with pressure arrows; a window cut-out highlighted
changes: cabin breathes in a 3.2 s cycle

explain.understand: every flight stretches the skin, then releases it

scenes.tts: Exhibit one: the cabin. In flight, it pushed outward at about eight pounds per square inch. Every flight stretched the skin.
scenes.caption: Exhibit one: the cabin.|In flight, it pushed outward|at about eight pounds per square inch.|Every flight stretched the skin.

scenes.subject: Exhibit 2: fuselage in a water tank, cycle counter 1,230 → 3,060, crack from a hatch corner

explain.understand: repeated pressurizing alone, with no storm or bomb, cracked the fuselage at a corner
explain.change: count rises until the skin splits

scenes.tts: Exhibit two. Investigators sank a whole Comet fuselage in a water tank and pumped it up and down, over and over. At about three thousand cycles, real flights included, the skin split... at an escape-hatch window corner.
scenes.caption: Exhibit two.|Investigators sank a whole Comet fuselage|in a water tank|and pumped it up and down, over and over.|At about three thousand cycles,|real flights included,|the skin split...|at an escape-hatch window corner.

scenes.subject: Exhibit 3: torn roof panel from the Elba wreck, window cut-out, fatigue beach marks ringed
changes: beach marks and red ring on 'fatigue'

explain.understand: the real crash started at the same kind of spot

scenes.tts: Exhibit three. Wreckage from off Elba pointed to the same kind of spot: a roof window cut-out, with marks of metal fatigue.
scenes.caption: Exhibit three.|Wreckage from off Elba|pointed to the same kind of spot:|a roof window cut-out,|with marks of metal fatigue.

scenes.subject: force-flow lines in a stretched skin detour around a cut-out and crowd at its corners

explain.understand: a hole concentrates force at the edge where it turns most sharply
explain.cause: load has to detour around the opening
text: force piles up where the edge turns

scenes.tts: Why corners? Force in the skin flows like traffic. A hole makes it detour, and it piles up where the edge turns.
scenes.caption: Why corners?|Force in the skin flows like traffic.|A hole makes it detour,|and it piles up where the edge turns.

scenes.subject: Inglis curve: peak stress factor vs tip radius; marker climbs from 3x as the hole sharpens
changes: tip radius shrinks, marker climbs toward 9x on 'tighter'

explain.understand: a round hole triples peak stress; tighter tips raise it fast
explain.change: marker climbs as the tip sharpens

scenes.tts: In a simple textbook model, a round hole triples the stress at its edge. Tighten the curve, and the peak keeps climbing.
scenes.caption: In a simple textbook model,|a round hole triples the stress at its edge.|Tighten the curve,|and the peak keeps climbing.

scenes.subject: the Comet 1 window drawn to scale (16.6 x 14 in) with its 3-inch corner radius highlighted; calc vs tests note

explain.understand: the myth is 'sharp square windows'; the fact is rounded corners that still ran far over the calculated stress, flexed every flight

scenes.tts: Here's what most retellings skip. The Comet's windows weren't sharp squares: a test report lists three-inch corner radii. But the stress there ran far higher than calculated.
scenes.caption: Here's what most retellings skip.|The Comet's windows weren't sharp squares:|a test report lists three-inch corner radii.|But the stress there ran far higher than calculated.

scenes.subject: squarish window morphs into an oval; a yellow highlighter traces its edge with no corner

explain.understand: the repeatable takeaway: no corner, no pile-up

scenes.tts: Later Comets got oval windows. So next flight, trace the window by your seat: no corner for the force to pile into. Follow for one bonus braincell per scroll.
scenes.caption: Later Comets got oval windows.|So next flight, trace the window by your seat:|no corner for the force to pile into.|Follow for one bonus braincell per scroll.
